content:
alex: FYI customer AcmePay hit duplicate side-effects after tool call retries. They reported two charges and two downstream webhooks fired for one prompt.

samir: ugh. any request ids or example payloads?

alex: yes — request_id r-0f3c9, conversation id conv-77. Relevant timeline: client sent generation+toolcall -> we returned 202 Accepted (no body, operation url) -> client retried after timeout -> second request came in and we executed the tool again. Customer says first run did actually succeed (charge created) but client retried and we re-ran create_charge.

devon: can you paste the original API/response? also is there an idempotency key header?

alex: paste below (redacted):
```http
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rwd-chat-1",
  "input": "charge customer for invoice",
  "functions": ["create_charge"],
  "metadata": {"customer_id":"acme-42"}
}

HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Location: /operations/op-9a2f
Retry-After: 3
```

alex: tool endpoint logs show two separate invocations: `create_charge invoice=inv-900, amount=2500` at 2026-02-14T12:02:11Z and again at 2026-02-14T12:02:15Z. Both succeeded. Billing shows two charges. No idempotency header present.

jess: is the root cause client-side retrying without idempotency? or did our gateway reproxy and resend?

devon: I instrumented the gateway trace. After 202 we reply quickly, trace shows reply left, but the client (Acme SDK) retried because it didn't see the operation status URL in their client path (they have a race where they expect immediate json body but we 202+location). Their retry sent an almost-identical POST to /v1/generate — not a repeat to /operations. So server treated it as a brand new request and routed to the same tool.

samir: That matches duplicate exec pattern. Two mitigations: enforce idempotency at tool layer (reject duplicate create_charge for same invoice id), and tweak API to return an operation id in response body too for common SDKs. Also add short-lived dedupe tokens in the request path.

billing: we need to reconcile charges with Acme. emergency refund for duplicate charge and a billing credit. I'll open a support ticket and escalate financial hold.

alex: customer asked if fallback interactions contributed — they saw in transcript the second run used the non-tool fallback path once (model returned plain text after the retry) but the tool execution still happened at infra level. Could that happen?

devon: possible if routing changed mid-retry: first request took path A (tool-run), second retried and policy selected fallback to non-tool for the model output, but the orchestrator had already enqueued the tool invocation. Our logs show the tool-run stage is decoupled and not fully gated by final model output validation, so there's room for race conditions.

samir: TL;DR root causes = client retry semantics + our 202 semantics + tool-run not idempotent + routing edge case where fallback didn't prevent a queued run.

jess: repro steps I used: 1) send POST that triggers long-tool action, our service returns 202 w/ Location, 2) immediately resend same POST (simulate client retry) 3) observe two tool invocations in tool logs. I can share a minimal curl script if you want.

alex: please paste curl script and also internal query to find all affected customers.

jess: curl script below (internal use):
```bash
# simulate client that retries on no-body 202
for i in 1 2; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","input":"charge","functions":["create_charge"],"metadata":{"invoice":"inv-900"}}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
```

jess: internal query to find similar incidents (run in kusto/logs):
```kusto
requests
| where url contains "/v1/generate" and status == 202 and tolower(headers) !contains "idempotency-key"
| extend rid=request_id, op=extract("op-[0-9a-f]+", 0, response_headers)
| join kind=inner (tool_logs | where tool_name=="create_charge") on rid
| summarize count() by op, customer_id
```

samir: action items: 1) P0 - support refund + billing credit (billing), 2) P1 - quick infra patch: include operation id in JSON body for 202 responses (devon), 3) P1 - add dedupe token support and require idempotency header passthrough to tools (samir), 4) P2 - audit where tool invocations are dispatched before model finalization (eng-runtime).

billing: started ticket BK-4523 and put hold on second charge; customer notified.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-085 (duplicate-tool-exec). Assigned to eng-oncall.

devon: I'll push a quick body-patch to API gateway to include `{"operation":"op-XXXX"}` in 202s and add a logged header `X-Operation-Id` for backcompat. Should reduce accidental client retries for common SDKs.

alex: thanks. Customer asked for ETA on refund and code fix. Billing ETA ~ 30m; dev ETA for gateway patch 4 hrs, full dedupe work ~ 5 days. I've communicated that.

samir: long-term: make tool endpoints idempotent by default for external side-effects; require idempotency-key in our public docs and SDKs. Also add a guard so fallback routing cancels pending tool enqueue if model output no longer requests it.

jess: putting repro + logs into the incident doc. will follow up with checklist for support.

alex: good work team. I'll close the loop with customer after refunds processed. :white_check_mark:
